source_region.content: Finite repeated game with one-based rounds t=1,...,T.
Adversary chooses y_t in [0,1] and keeps it secret.
Learner predicts x_t in [0,1] before observing the current outcome.
Outcome is revealed and the squared difference (x_t-y_t)^2 is charged.

source_region.locator: Let us start paragraph, first sentences
source_region.content: A fixed distribution over [0,1] is chosen initially; observations are independent and identically distributed, and the distribution is unknown to the learner.
Predicting the mean each round gives expected total sigma^2 T; source asserts no admissible learner can do better.
E_{Y_1,...,Y_T}[sum_t(x_t-Y_t)^2]-sigma^2 T; no explicit seed or sigma-field appears in the notation.
Expected total squared loss divided by T, minus sigma^2; an equivalent normalization for positive horizons.
Both excess quantities are asserted nonnegative; no conditioning or cross-term calculation is printed.
Successful strategy means sublinear total excess, equivalently average excess tends to zero; this is a criterion, not a claim that any learner succeeds.
More general game allows arbitrary outcomes, even chosen after the adversary observes the learner action. This is an adversarial setting boundary, not an IID independence premise.
Future unavailable; past known; use a predictor determined by past information.

nodes.description: Source asserts mean-oracle risk without displaying the mean/variance expansion or feasibility of the mean.
No explicit causal-information independence or expected cross-term argument is printed. The no-better assertion needs admissibility, not bounded predictions alone.
Division identity and asymptotic equivalence are asserted without proof. Inventoried for complete page coverage but outside the four targets.

nodes.description: Supplied source contains no sigma-field completion, modulo-ae measurable set definition, or real-valued version theorem. This is added general measure theory, not an omitted author theorem.
Private seed, generated information sigma field, measurable factorization, null-set modification and common event are explicit formal-model extensions absent from the source.
The supplied pages do not characterize a minimum/sInf of expected fixed losses. Its equality to T variance requires a derived proof from the source mean benchmark, with minimum outside expectation.
Under Measurable with respect to eventuallyMeasurableSpace F (ae mu), each real Borel preimage agrees a.e. with an F-measurable set. Use a countable determining family such as rational sublevel sets.
Choose representatives for the countable real determining family and intersect their equality events. Countably many a.e. assertions are equivalent to one a.e. assertion holding for all members.

Construct an F-measurable real version from coherent rational cuts, or prove the equivalent real standard-Borel version theorem. Resolve inconsistent cuts on an F-measurable bad set with a total value while showing this set is null; preserve equality a.e. No boundedness, probability, F<=ambient or finite-measure premise may be added.

The supplied eventuallyMeasurableSpace definition means: a set s belongs iff some F-measurable set r satisfies s= r modulo ae mu. F is not assumed below the ambient measurable space. Do not silently identify this with completion of a restricted measure.
H_t(omega)=(S(omega),(Y_i(omega))_{i in range t}); privateSeedPastInformation is comap H_t of product measurability. F_t<=this is an information inclusion, not a monotone-filtration axiom.

An F_t-measurable real version with F_t<=comap H_t factors measurably through H_t. Verify the exact real-valued measurable factorization theorem or prove it; arbitrary Seed has only its supplied measurable-space structure.

Clamp each factor measurably into [0,1] on all seed-history pairs. Original prediction bounds and version equality hold a.e., so this preserves realized predictions a.e.; off-support histories and null-set values may change.

After choosing one policy family, countably intersect per-time agreement/boundedness events. AE omega FORALL t and FORALL t AE omega are equivalent for natural times, not a stronger mathematical condition.

iIndepFun Y and seed independent of the whole stream yield independence of joint seed-plus-past H_t from Y_t. Disjoint range t excludes current index; pairwise independence cannot replace these joint premises.
Push joint independence through the measurable real-valued history factor; no prediction boundedness is required.
Alternative: prove current draw independent of seed-plus-past information sigma field, restrict to F, and apply to an F-measurable version. This avoids explicit policy factorization.
Independence is invariant under a.e. equality of the prediction. Transfer from the measurable version to the original completed-measurable P.
For T3/T4, measurable S and each Y make H_t ambient-measurable; F<=comap then makes its real versions ambient-measurable. This is not an assumption or requirement of T1/T2.
Probability measure and a.s. [0,1] observation/prediction bounds give integrability of all squares, centered products and finite sums; a.e. versions supply required measurability.
m=integral Y_0 lies in [0,1]; v=E[(Y_0-m)^2]. Identical laws transfer first and second moments to each Y_t. Same-law marginals alone suffice for the fixed-comparator identity.
Expand E[(P-Y_t)^2] as E[(P-m)^2]+v-2 E[(P-m)(Y_t-m)]. Independence and integrability factor the last term; E[Y_t-m]=0 makes it vanish.
For constant u in [0,1], expected total loss=T*(v+(u-m)^2). Nonempty bounded-below image attains Tv at feasible m, proving its sInf equals Tv without exchanging minimum and expectation.
Apply linearity of integrals of finite integrable sums, subtract the fixed benchmark Tv, and obtain sum_{t<T}E[(prediction_t-m)^2].
Every squared-error integral is nonnegative; hence its finite sum is nonnegative.
At T=0 finite sums vanish and the fixed-loss image is {0}; its sInf and regret are0. At t=0 the history is empty and only the seed can enter a policy.

Optional alternative to the direct version route: use the bounded explicit policy of T2, prove its risk identity by joint independence, then transfer the integrals back using a.e. equality. This is derived analysis, not a printed proof or verified library invocation.

routes.premise_discharge: Retains the omitted mean-risk and no-better causal argument; not a printed proof chain.
Information order must prevent access to current draw. Source does not specify null sets, completion or private seed.
Positive-horizon normalization; not a Batch28 target and not used to conclude convergence for T4.
Unfold supplied modulo-ae set definition for countably many real Borel generators; hP supplies each completed-measurable preimage.
Countable determining real sets permit one coherent F-measurable reconstruction agreeing with P a.e.; exact reconstruction proof remains an obligation. Arbitrary mu and F retained.
Apply T1 separately at each time. F_t inclusion gives measurability with respect to H_t comap, so derive a measurable factor. No ambient measurability of H_t is needed here.
Original a.s. prediction bounds preserve clamped agreement; the constructed factor is bounded on every q, including unrealized histories. Countability produces common event.
Use unbounded factorization of an F-measurable version at fixed t, transport current-draw independence, and transfer a.e. equality. Does not invoke the bounded T2 theorem.
Prove information/current-draw independence using hind and hseed, restrict to F, apply to version, then transfer a.e. Equality. No factorized policy necessary.
Bounded same-law marginals give scalar quadratic expected fixed loss. Mean is feasible and attains minimum, discharging nonempty/bounded-below sInf conditions internally.
Instantiate T3 at each t, then use product-integral factorization and zero mean of Y_t-m. Identity not a public premise.
Interchange only finite sums and integrals with integrability; cancel Tv. Infimum stays outside expectation.
Exact identity plus nonnegative integrals. T=0 is explicit; no asymptotic claim.

Apply measurable-image independence to T2 policy, expand its risk, subtract expected fixed minimum, and transport by a.e. equality. A separate sufficient route rather than an extra AND dependency of R-DIRECT.
